**1 — Scene:** Three pieces of topped toast: two appear to have scrambled eggs with herbs, and the upper piece appears to have beans or a chunky vegetable topping, a little soft white cheese, and rocket. The dim lighting makes the toppings somewhat uncertain.

**2 — Vessel:** A round dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** across. Area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Toast, scrambled eggs with chopped herbs, a bean/vegetable mixture, soft white cheese, and rocket. No separate pool of oil or dressing is clearly visible. For calculation, I treat each toast and its main topping as a composite item, avoiding double-counting their overlapping footprints.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:**

| Item as plated | Plate area | Area × average height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated grams | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Scrambled-egg toast, two pieces | 43% | 228 × 1.8 = 410 ml | 0.80 g/ml | 328 | 190 | 623 kcal |
| Bean/vegetable toast | 26% | 138 × 1.6 = 221 ml | 0.85 g/ml | 188 | 180 | 338 kcal |
| Soft white cheese | 2% | 11 × 1.0 = 11 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 11 | 250 | 28 kcal |
| Rocket garnish | 1% | 5 × 2.0 = 10 ml | 0.15 g/ml | 2 | 25 | 1 kcal |

The allocated areas total **72% of the plate**, consistent with the visible coverage. Garnish areas are allocated separately rather than counted again in the toast footprints. Composite densities account for the bread and toppings together; no additional gap reduction is applied.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **529 g and 990 kcal** is plausible for three generously topped toast pieces. The garnish contributes only a few grams. Given the uncertain topping identities and thickness, a reasonable uncertainty is roughly ±25%.
